title: Publish 0.6.2 to npm — tagged, qualified and receipt-verified; awaiting the user's authorisation
description:
0.6.2 is tagged, qualified and receipt-verified. ONLY the npm publish remains, and it needs a HUMAN AT A REAL TERMINAL -- npm demands a browser OTP that cannot complete in a non-TTY. Do not attempt it from an agent session.

=== ALREADY VERIFIED. DO NOT RE-DERIVE OR RE-RUN ANY OF THIS ===

  Tag v0.6.2            -> commit ea3813ae39fd9c9bba1e5e24e32a4c73e1611480
  That commit is the tip main was promoted to, and remains an ancestor of main.
  Qualification run      34801853367 (attempt 3), conclusion: success
  Receipt                schema lore.ladybug-qualification-evidence/1
                         repository.commit = ea3813ae39fd9c9bba1e5e24e32a4c73e1611480
                         status = pass
  Receipt verified INDEPENDENTLY, not merely read: the concurrency evidence
  artifact was downloaded and its sha256 recomputed as
  dae6a2773720be84676dce3da57ac37db4c90979b58935e662c3c817b569b70a,
  which matches the digest the receipt claims, byte for byte. A self-consistent
  receipt proves nothing about what was built; this one attests real bytes from
  the shipped commit.
  The LCLI-481 provenance gate ran and behaved: --pre success on every attempt,
  --post correctly skipped because nothing published.

These are settled facts. A successor re-running qualification would burn ~25
minutes to learn what is written above.

=== THE PUBLISH, READY TO PASTE ===

The artifacts are NOT on disk, and CI does NOT produce SHA256SUMS.txt -- the
operator generates it (see the WARNING below about what that check does and does
not prove).

    cd /Volumes/external/repos/lore-cli
    gh run download 34801853367 -n npm-packages -D scripts/release-0.6.2
    cd scripts/release-0.6.2 && shasum -a 256 *.tgz > SHA256SUMS.txt && cd -
    ls scripts/release-0.6.2/*.tgz | wc -l          # must be 7
    scripts/publish-release.sh 0.6.2 34801853367 --dry-run    # rehearse; touches nothing
    scripts/publish-release.sh 0.6.2 34801853367              # the real publish

AUTH: a granular or automation npm token read from the macOS Keychain (service
npm-opum-ai-publish), falling back to NPM_TOKEN then ~/.npmrc. `npm login` does
NOT work here: a web login is still subject to require-2FA-on-write, which is
exactly the EOTP wall the token exists to bypass. The browser OTP step is why
this needs a person at a TTY.

ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: six platform packages first, root launcher LAST, so the
launcher is never resolvable before the binary it execs. Fail-closed -- a
platform failure stops BEFORE the launcher, so a partial publish leaves nothing
installable and the same version can be retried. Resumable: an already-published
package is skipped rather than re-attempted.

AFTER PUBLISHING, DO NOT PANIC AT A SLOW REGISTRY. LCLI-460 shipped in this
release: the script now waits up to 30 minutes with backoff before the install
smoke and states explicitly that a timeout is NOT proof the publish failed. The
lag is real and worsening -- 0.4.5 ~15s, 0.4.6 ~35s, 0.5.0 ~25 MINUTES. NEVER
reach for `npm unpublish` on a propagation delay; it is destructive, available
for 72 hours, and the wrong tool for this.

=== WARNING: THE DIGEST CHECK IS CIRCULAR ===

publish-release.sh advertises "verifies every tarball's sha256 against
SHA256SUMS.txt BEFORE publishing anything". CI never emits that file, so the
operator generates it from the very tarballs it then verifies. That proves only
that the files have not changed since `shasum` ran -- NOT that they are the
qualified artifacts. Treat the check as a tamper-evidence seal on your own
download, not as provenance. Making it real needs digests CI recorded
independently. Not yet filed as a task; it needs a decision about the source of
truth, not just an edit.

=== AFTER A SUCCESSFUL PUBLISH ===

1. Update the post-publish evidence, which was deliberately NOT touched at bump
   time because both files state what is published NOW: README.md and
   docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md.
2. Cut a GitHub Release for v0.6.2 using CHANGELOG.md's [0.6.2] section.
3. Tell opum-marketplace that npm dist-tags.latest has actually moved. They are
   deliberately HOLDING their opum-lore pin at v0.6.1 until it does, because
   pinning ahead of npm would point the skill at a release nobody can install.
   They already have the skills/ tree SHA 24277e9a94d6cc9b5a8c7fa12fa32c4f15eb4c0f
   and have recorded in their own memory to check `npm view @opum-ai/lore
   dist-tags` themselves rather than wait for a message.
4. 0.6.2 ships with NO provenance attestation, as 0.6.1 did (LCLI-482, open).
   Say so wherever the release is announced rather than letting someone find it
   in the packument and read it as tampering.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A published @opum-ai/lore 0.6.2 exists on the registry with dist-tags.latest at 0.6.2, verified by `npm view @opum-ai/lore dist-tags` rather than by the publish command exiting 0
All seven packages are live -- the six platform packages and the root launcher -- and a clean-registry `npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@0.6.2 --version` reports 0.6.2
README.md and docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md are updated to state 0.6.2 as the published version, which was deliberately deferred from the bump because they assert what is published now
A GitHub Release exists for v0.6.2 carrying CHANGELOG.md 0.6.2 section
opum-marketplace is told that dist-tags.latest actually moved, so it can lift its deliberate hold at v0.6.1
The release is recorded as having shipped WITHOUT a provenance attestation, so nobody later reads the absence as tampering (LCLI-482 remains open)

implementationNotes:
AUTH DESCRIPTION IN THIS RECORD IS WRONG — CORRECTED 2026-09-14, before any fourth publish attempt.

This task says auth is "a granular or automation npm token read from the macOS Keychain (service
npm-opum-ai-publish), falling back to NPM_TOKEN then ~/.npmrc". Checked on this machine, with the
user's explicit go-ahead for a presence-only inspection that printed no values:

  - Keychain service npm-opum-ai-publish : ABSENT. `security find-generic-password -s
    npm-opum-ai-publish` exits 44, "could not be found in the keychain".
  - NPM_TOKEN                            : NOT SET.
  - ~/.npmrc                             : EXISTS and contains //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken
                                           (plus //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken, an
                                           @evolvconsulting:registry line, and allow-scripts).

So both documented primary paths are unused. The publish authenticates with whatever token sits in
~/.npmrc — the script's LAST fallback, not its designed one.

WHY THAT LIKELY EXPLAINS THE OTP WALL, stated as the inference it is rather than as a measurement.
`npm login` writes exactly that `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken` line, and a web-login session
remains subject to "require 2FA for writes". publish-release.sh:5-8 names this precisely as the EOTP
wall the Keychain token exists to bypass. An unattended publish was therefore never actually
configured on this machine — the OTP prompt is the documented behaviour of the fallback that is in
use, not a surprise.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the question that decides whether the wall is removable: whether that
~/.npmrc token is a granular access token or a web-login session token. Reading the token would not
settle it either (both carry the npm_ prefix). The decisive read-only checks are `npm whoami` — a 401
would mean expired or revoked rather than 2FA-gated — or simply looking at npmjs.com. Neither was run:
they authenticate as the user, which is past the presence-only scope that was authorised.

ALSO STALE, relevant to any reader of the script: publish-release.sh:5-8 offers "a GRANULAR ACCESS
TOKEN (or classic Automation token)". docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md:557-565 records that npm
permanently revoked every classic token on 9 December 2025, leaving granular tokens as the only type
(90-day cap, 2FA-bound, website-only creation). If the runbook holds, the automation-token option no
longer exists and cannot be chosen.

CHANGE NO CREDENTIAL on this note's account. Credential setup is tier 3 and belongs to the user
directly. Recorded as a fact so attempt four is not spent rediscovering it. Follow-on work: LCLI-489.
